title: Residency compliance dossier generator for dedicated tenants
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Build a service that compiles a per-tenant compliance dossier for Dedicated customers. The dossier should bundle tenant residency assertions, retention configuration, relevant audit logs (access, admin actions, data exports), and a signed machine-readable manifest plus a PDF human-readable report. The generator must support scheduled monthly exports and on-demand generation from the Console or via the Compliance API. The output must be stored in the customer-specific compliance archive (S3 bucket or on-prem equivalent) and include cryptographic signatures (KMS/HSM) and a verification endpoint. This ticket covers design and implementation of the first iteration: generator service, manifest schema, KMS signing integration, storage/retention policy enforcement, Console link, and end-to-end integration test against a dedicated tenant sandbox.
acceptance_criteria: Given a dedicated tenant with residency tags, when a dossier is generated, then the archive contains: signed_manifest.json, human_report.pdf, audit_log_segment.ndjson
Manifest must include residency_region, node_ids, storage_locations, retention_policy_ids, generation_timestamp, generator_version
Signed manifest must be verifiable via the new /compliance/verify endpoint using Redwood public key
Console must surface the latest dossier with a signed download link that expires (pre-signed URL)
Scheduled monthly job triggers generation and retention enforcement does not delete evidence required by retention policy
E2E integration test covers KMS sign/verify flow and upload to compliance archive with expected metadata tags
design_notes: Prefer a small standalone generator service (compliance-dossier-svc) that reads from the residency index and retention config store
Use existing tenant snapshot service to collect node and placement data, but add additional fields: instance_fingerprint and model_variant_hash
Manifest schema v1 should be JSON-LD-ish to make assertions machine-readable by auditors. Schema: flat fields + arrays; avoid nesting beyond one level to simplify signing
Signing: integrate with KMS-backed signer (use dedicated-kms key alias: alias/redwood/compliance/dedicated). The signer returns signature+key_id for embedding in manifest
Storage: upload artifacts to s3://redwood-compliance-archive/<tenant_id>/<YYYY-MM>/ and apply lifecycle rules; include object tags: tenant_id, dossier_version, region
Verification endpoint to validate signature, manifest hash, and return a short verification report for auditors. Rate-limit and log access to verification endpoint for audit trail
implementation_plan: API: POST /api/v1/tenants/:id/dossiers - triggers on-demand generation; GET /api/v1/tenants/:id/dossiers/:version - fetch metadata
Worker: generator reads residency index (read replica), retention config service, and audit-log-collector export for the time window
KMS integration: use kms-client v2 library; implement retry/backoff and idempotency for signing calls
Storage: emit upload events to object-metadata-queue and ensure event contains signed_manifest checksum for downstream verification
Console: add a Dossiers panel under Security -> Compliance for Dedicated tenants with last-run status and download button
Tests: unit tests for schema, integration test for KMS signing (use test key), and an E2E test that runs against a dedicated sandbox tenant
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Large audit log exports could exceed memory/time budget -> Mitigation: stream NDJSON segments and slice by time windows
Risk: KMS rate limits during bulk generation -> Mitigation: implement signing queue with concurrency cap and fallback to async signing mode
Risk: Sensitive data leaked in human_report PDF -> Mitigation: redact PII fields and ensure docs follow retention config before generation
Risk: Cross-region storage complexity for residency -> Mitigation: respect residency_region in storage path and maintain read-only replica mapping
